construction_markdown:
Let
\[
p(Z)=Z^{16}+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1,
\qquad F=\mathbb F_2[Z]/(p),
\]
and put \(\alpha=Z\bmod p\). Write every \(z\in F\) uniquely as \(z=\sum_{i=0}^{15}z_i\alpha^i\).

Fix
\[
A=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F_2}\{1,\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^{14}\},
\qquad Y=\mathbb F_2^{15}.
\]
Order both sets by increasing binary coefficient integer. Define
\[
H(z)_y=z_0+\sum_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i,
\qquad y=(y_1,\ldots,y_{15})\in Y.
\]
Thus \(H\) is the explicit additive identification of \(F\) with \(\operatorname{RM}(1,15)\).

For
\[
f(X)=\sum_{j=0}^{64}c_jX^j\in F[X],
\]
define
\[
C(f)=\bigl(H(f(a))_y\bigr)_{(a,y)\in A\times Y},
\qquad
C=\{C(f):\deg f\le64\}.
\]
Coordinates are ordered first by \(a\), then by \(y\). There is no padding, puncturing, sampling, or unspecified constituent code. The candidate remains under review pending formal campaign acceptance.

discussion_posts.body_markdown:
For the affine encoder \(H(z)_y=z_0+\sum_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i\), any outer vector \(u\in F^N\) satisfies
\[
W(H^N(u))=2^{15}(N_0(u)-N_1(u)),\qquad
\operatorname{wt}(H^N(u))=2^{14}(N-N_0(u)+N_1(u)).
\]
At \(N=32768\), the target is exactly \(N_0-N_1\le64\); it becomes \(|N_0-N_1|\le64\) when complements are present.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Let \(W\le F^{32768}\) be any \(F\)-linear outer code whose affine-inner descent meets the target. Applying the target inequality to \(t^{-1}w\) gives \(N_0(w)-N_t(w)\le64\) for every \(t\ne0\). If \(N_0(w)\ge65\), every one of the 65535 nonzero symbols must occur, impossible in 32768 positions. Hence the outer distance is at least 32704, and Singleton gives \(\dim_F W\le65\). Thus binary dimension 1040 is the exact ceiling for this entire field-linear outer architecture.

discussion_posts.body_markdown:
Does a deterministic binary \([32768,18,16381]\) inner code exist? Concatenating it with an outer \([32768,59,32710]_{2^{18}}\) Reed–Solomon code would give
\[
[2^{30},1062,\ge535822510]_2,
\]
beating the target by 174. Griesmer only gives \(g_2(18,16381)=32766\), so it does not exclude this defect-two inner code. Such an inner code cannot contain \(\operatorname{RM}(1,15)\): an added coset would require every Walsh coefficient to have magnitude at most 6, contradicting Parseval.

proof_markdown:
## Theorem

The construction above is a deterministic binary linear code with exact parameters
\[
[2^{30},1040,535{,}822{,}336]_2.
\]

## Field certificate

Repeated squaring modulo
\[
p(Z)=Z^{16}+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1
\]
gives
\[
Z^{256}\equiv Z^8+Z^7+Z^3+Z,
\qquad Z^{65536}\equiv Z.
\]
Thus \(Z^{256}+Z\equiv h:=Z^8+Z^7+Z^3\). Direct division over \(\mathbb F_2[Z]\) gives
\[
p=(Z^8+Z^7+Z^6+Z^5+Z^4+Z^2+1)h+(Z^2+1),
\]
\[
h=(Z^6+Z^5+Z^4+Z^3+Z^2+1)(Z^2+1)+1.
\]
Hence \(\gcd(p,Z^{256}+Z)=1\). Together with \(Z^{65536}\equiv Z\), Rabin's degree-16 criterion proves that \(p\) is irreducible. Therefore \(F\) is the explicitly represented field of order \(2^{16}\).

## Inner Fourier calculation

The map \(H\) is binary linear and injective: \(H(z)=0\) evaluated at \(y=0\) gives \(z_0=0\), and evaluation at the fifteen unit vectors then gives \(z_1=\cdots=z_{15}=0\).

For fixed \(z\), character orthogonality gives
\[
\sum_{y\in Y}(-1)^{H(z)_y}=
\begin{cases}
2^{15},&z=0,\\
-2^{15},&z=1,\\
0,&z\notin\{0,1\}.
\end{cases}
\]
Indeed, the last case has a nonzero linear coefficient, and pairing \(y\) with \(y+e_i\) cancels the terms. Thus \(H(F)=\operatorname{RM}(1,15)\) has parameters \([32768,16,16384]_2\).

For an outer vector \(u\), write \(N_t(u)=|\{a:u_a=t\}|\). Its concatenated Walsh sum and weight are exactly
\[
W(u)=2^{15}(N_0(u)-N_1(u)),
\]
\[
\operatorname{wt}(H^A(u))
=2^{14}(32768-N_0(u)+N_1(u)).
\]

## Binary linearity, length, and dimension

Polynomial evaluation and \(H\) are binary linear, so \(C\) is binary linear. Its coordinate set has size
\[
|A||Y|=2^{15}2^{15}=2^{30}.
\]
The message space has \(65\) coefficients in \(F\), hence binary dimension \(65\cdot16=1040\). The encoder is injective: if \(C(f)=0\), injectivity of \(H\) gives \(f(a)=0\) at all \(32768\) points of \(A\). A polynomial of degree at most 64 with that many roots is zero.

## Minimum distance

Let \(f\) be nonconstant. Both \(f\) and \(f-1\) are nonzero polynomials of degree at most 64, so
\[
N_0(f)\le64,
\qquad N_1(f)\le64.
\]
Consequently
\[
|W(C(f))|
=2^{15}|N_0(f)-N_1(f)|
\le64\cdot2^{15}=2^{21},
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{wt}(C(f))
\ge\frac{2^{30}-2^{21}}2
=2^{29}-2^{20}
=535{,}822{,}336.
\]
The nonzero constant \(f=1\) gives the all-one word; any other nonzero constant gives balanced inner blocks. Hence every nonzero codeword is covered.

The bound is attained. Let \(R\) be the first 64 points of \(A\), and put
\[
g(X)=\prod_{r\in R}(X-r).
\]
Every value in \(g(A\setminus R)\) is nonzero, and this image has at most \(32704<65535=|F^*|\) elements. Let \(z\) be the first element of \(F^*\setminus g(A\setminus R)\), and set \(f=z^{-1}g\). Then \(f\) has exactly 64 zeros on \(A\) and never equals 1 elsewhere. Its remaining 32704 blocks are nonconstant affine words of weight \(2^{14}\). Therefore
\[
\operatorname{wt}(C(f))=32704\cdot2^{14}=535{,}822{,}336,
\]
proving the exact minimum distance.

## Optimality within the field-linear outer architecture

Let \(W\le F^{32768}\) be any \(F\)-linear outer code whose blockwise image under \(H\) meets the target. For every nonzero \(w\in W\), the exact weight formula implies
\[
N_0(w)-N_1(w)\le64.
\]
For any \(t\in F^*\), apply this to \(t^{-1}w\). Scaling preserves its zero fiber and sends its \(t\)-fiber to the 1-fiber, so
\[
N_0(w)-N_t(w)\le64.
\]
If \(N_0(w)\ge65\), then \(N_t(w)\ge1\) for all 65535 nonzero \(t\), forcing at least \(65+65535>32768\) coordinates. Thus every nonzero outer word has at most 64 zeros, and the outer Hamming distance is at least 32704.

Puncturing any 32703 coordinates is therefore injective on \(W\), giving
\[
|W|\le |F|^{65},
\qquad \dim_F W\le65.
\]
Hence binary dimension 1040 is optimal for every \(F\)-linear outer code with this affine inner encoder.
